newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent dull, refiners mop up other grades.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent dull, refiners mop up other grades.

text.p: North Sea Brent spot and paper market trade was extremely thin, but refiners continued to mop up other North Sea crudes at attractive prices, traders said.
Forties cargoes traded 7-8 cents weaker at Dated Brent +8 and +7 cents for early October barrels with the prompt supply overhang keeping refiners in the driving seat.
Early October Statfjord barrels were heard sold at Dated Brent +10 cents and Ekofisk barrels for end Sept traded down at dated Brent +3/-4 cents compared with +15 cents done Tuesday.
Dated Brent was valued steady at Nov paper +12 cents with the Oct/Nov spread on offer at +55 cents in late business.

Traders said spread values had weakened a little over the day as weaker futures markets trimmed outright values for forward paper contracts. November paper was assessed around 25 cents weaker at $21.95/$22.05 in late business.
While the spot market overhang pegged Dated Brent in steep contango, further forward the spread curve appeared to flattening out in a bid-ask range between +52 and +60 cents.
"The market is holding and seems to be rangebound at these levels," a paper trader said.
With the front end of the market in contango, dealers expected to see the overhang of September cargoes disappear.
"It beats the cost of storage if you can buy at a contango discount to paper," a trader for a European oil company said.
Traders said improved refinery margins and strong gas oil demand this side of the Atlantic could see sweet grades easily absorbed by refineries replenishing winter stocks.
However, CFD levels for next week's dates were slightly softer on the day at Nov +18/+21 cents, indicating some weakening in sentiment.
In the Mediterranean sour crude markets were firm but thin as traders waited for next month's Russian Urals programme to be released and for October Syrian prices to be settled.
Sytrol on Thursday repeated its offer of Dated Brent -30 cents for Syrian Light crude liftings in October, an increase of 10 cents over September.
"We haven't responded yet but it's something we can't accept at the moment," said a term lifter. Most lifters said they were looking for a rollover of September's prices.

The Urals market was "dead" ahead of the release of the October programme, expected next week. A Sept 27-29 cargo was rumoured to have been sold on Wednesday at Dated Brent -80 cents but details could not be confirmed, traders said.
Improved refinery margins were also helping sweet distillate-rich crudes. Algeria raised the price of its Saharan Blend by nine cents to Dated Brent +70 cents for October.
